icons.source: scripts/extract_card_icons.py, harvested from the 54 card fronts already in public/cards/ -- nothing uploaded, nothing fetched. plantdex.online is proxy-blocked from this sandbox and did not need to be reached.
icons.how_labelled: Each front carries exactly two discs in two fixed slots, and herbs.json lists that card's two uses IN ORDER. Labels come from that cross-reference, not from somebody deciding what a picture means -- then every instance is re-classified against the medoids to check the ordering assumption actually holds.
icons.agreement: 85/90 use discs and 45/45 season tiles land on their own label. The five that do not all involve topical/bone/wound/energy, which are genuinely similar at the 48px grey resolution the check compares at. All twelve were then verified BY EYE against the rendered set and every label is correct: bone=joint, calm=seated figure, digestive=stomach, edible=fork and knife, energy=bolt, heart=heart with pulse, immune=shield, lungs=lungs, tea=steaming cup, topical=open hand, urinary=kidneys, wound=bandage.

review_flags.reason: No sourced water/sun/temperature values, so no droplet, sun or thermometer icons are drawn. The printed deck counts these off its own artwork; for a generated species they need a horticultural source. The icons exist and are ready.
No sourced value. GBIF occurrence counts are the obvious basis; the mapping from a count to Common/Uncommon/Rare/Epic is a product decision nobody has made.

All four season icons are now extracted, but NOTHING RETRIEVED SUPPORTS A SEASON for this species. The eight CC0 observations run April, April, May, May, August, September, September, September across Spain, Italy, Hungary, Russia and the UK -- too few, too scattered and too spread in latitude to call a season. Eight photos are not phenology. A flora or a GBIF phenology query would settle it.
digestive and calm, both carried by approved-standing claims (the Lithuanian ethnobotany record and the Iranian survey's anxiety use). The deck gives every printed card exactly two.
Chamomile is a summer species, but only the WINTER snowflake has been extracted. The spring/summer/autumn icons are missing.
A taste note is an observation by somebody holding the plant, not a citation. Blank.

One claim refused: the sesquiterpenoid list (chamazulene, alpha-bisabolol) was drafted at laboratory standing but its source sits in the documented-use query group, which can only support traditional. Probably true; the rule still refuses it.

The hero is a GrabCut cut-out and keeps a small artefact of stem at the upper right. No learned matte was used: a classical cut fails visibly, where a model can invent a plausible edge that is not the plant's.
